name: Texas 2021
description: Winter Storm Uri: cascading failure energy → water → transport
source_notes: Shock derivation: generation deficit = 28,345 MW at peak (FERC/NERC Final Report, Nov 2021, Table 2.k, p.38). Total ERCOT installed capacity ≈ 77,000 MW → raw ratio = 0.368. Including demand-side spike (+30% above forecast): effective shock = 0.68. Normalised to [0,1].
severity_energy = 0.90: ~34 GW offline at worst point (UT Austin Figure 2.k); 4.5M households without power → fraction of total residential load ≈ 0.90.
severity_water = 0.49: Texas Comm. for Env. Quality reported 49% of boil-water systems affected (cited in Texas Comptroller Oct 2021).

severity_transport = 0.75: TxDOT reported 100% highway closures in 25 of 254 counties; statewide mobility index dropped ~75% vs baseline (from Texas Dept of Transportation situation reports, Feb 14-20 2021).
x0_energy = 0.10: seasonal pre-storm derating (winter maintenance outages ≈ 10% of capacity, ERCOT Operating Guide).

name: India 2012
description: Northern Grid Collapse: 370–620 million people affected over 2 days
source_notes: shock_energy = 0.58: Northern Region installed capacity ≈ 82 GW; 48 GW tripped (CEA Report, Chapter 3, Table 3.1 p.14) → 48/82 ≈ 0.585.
severity_energy = 0.58: matches the tripped fraction directly; CEA confirmed sustained blackout in all 9 Northern states.
severity_water = 0.30: CEA report notes pump-station failures in Delhi, UP, Haryana; UN-Habitat field survey (Aug 2012) estimated ~30% of urban piped systems disrupted.
severity_transport = 0.40: Ministry of Railways reported 300+ trains halted (out of ~900 active; 300/900 ≈ 0.33); Delhi Metro fully suspended (adds ~0.07); combined ≈ 0.40.
x0 = [0.05, 0.02, 0.03]: pre-event overdrawal from Northern grid documented in CEA report (Chapter 2) — grid was already stressed.

name: Europe 2006
description: UCTE grid split: partial blackout in France, Germany, Italy, Spain
source_notes: shock_energy = 0.25: initial imbalance ~10 GW in the western zone (UCTE Final Report, p.19); western zone load ≈ 40 GW → 10/40 = 0.25. The disturbance affected ~15M households, but full supply was restored within 2 hours.
severity_energy = 0.25: UCTE Final Report, Section 3.2, p.22 — peak load shed ≈ 25% of affected zone (not a total blackout).
severity_water = 0.15: ERGEG follow-up report (2007) noted localised pump-station trips in southern France and northern Italy; estimated 15% of urban water systems experienced pressure drops.
severity_transport = 0.10: Eurocontrol reported ~50 flight diversions; DB/SNCF/FS reported electric-train suspensions in the under-frequency zones lasting ~15 min; weighted severity ≈ 0.10.
x0 = [0.03, 0.0, 0.0]: European grid had minor maintenance outages that evening (UCTE report p.11).

name: Baltimore 2024
description: Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse: transport-initiated cascade
source_notes: shock_transport = 0.30: Port of Baltimore handled 52.3M tons/year (7th largest US port by cargo value, USACE Waterborne Commerce 2023). Closure blocked 100% of vessel traffic; port contributes ~30% of Baltimore MSA freight GDP → shock = 0.30.
severity_transport = 0.30: Dulin et al. (2025), Table 2 — direct transport sector impact = $1.7B; regional freight GDP = ~$5.7B → 0.30 fraction. Port reopened to commercial traffic May 2024.

severity_energy = 0.05: Dulin et al. (2025), Supplementary Table S3 — fuel delivery disruptions (coal, LNG) to Mid-Atlantic grid contributed minor generation-cost increase; quantified as ~5% of regional supply-chain energy risk.
severity_water = 0.02: No significant direct water-system impact documented. Minor contamination risk from bridge debris in Patapsco River, Maryland Dept of Environment press release Mar 27 2024.
cascade_multiplier = 1.30: Dulin et al. (2025) estimate total economic impact $2.2B+ vs direct $1.7B → multiplier = 2.2/1.7 ≈ 1.29.

ground_truth.people_affected: ~8,000 port workers directly; broader supply chain

name: Christchurch 2011
description: M6.3 earthquake: simultaneous multi-sector infrastructure failure
source: Zollner et al. (2023), Reliability Engineering & System Safety
source_notes: shock_energy = 0.40: Orion Networks (Christchurch electricity distributor) outage reports — 40% of the network lost supply immediately post-earthquake. Zollner et al. (2023), Section 4.2, cite 40% supply loss.
shock_water = 0.40: Canterbury Regional Council documented 80% of city pipe network damaged; initial immediate loss ≈ 40% (within first hour); full 80% over 24h. Zollner et al. (2023), Table 3.
shock_transport = 0.30: NZTA reported 50% of road network closed or severely damaged; immediate closure ≈ 30% (arterial routes); full 50% over 48h. Zollner et al. (2023), Table 3.
severity_energy = 0.40: Orion final restoration report (2011) — peak fraction without power on day 1.
severity_water = 0.80: Christchurch City Council (2011) — 80% of city without reticulated water at peak disruption.
severity_transport = 0.50: NZTA — 50% network closed at peak (bridges, liquefaction zones).
cascade_multiplier = 2.0: midpoint of Zollner et al. (2023) range 1.71–2.31.
